front_blocks.md: Define **user-defined data type**.

back_blocks.md: A user-defined data type is a **custom data type created by the programmer**, built from existing types to match the specific needs of a program.

cards.front_md: Define **user-defined data type**.
cards.back_md: A user-defined data type is a **custom data type created by the programmer**, built from existing types to match the specific needs of a program.

front_blocks.md: Name three things user-defined types let you do.

back_blocks.md: Group **related data** under a single identifier, restrict a variable to a **fixed set of valid values**, and build **dynamic data structures** such as linked lists.

cards.front_md: Name three things user-defined types let you do.
cards.back_md: Group **related data** under a single identifier, restrict a variable to a **fixed set of valid values**, and build **dynamic data structures** such as linked lists.

front_blocks.md: Define **non-composite data type**.

back_blocks.md: A non-composite data type is a type defined **without referencing another data type**.

cards.front_md: Define **non-composite data type**.
cards.back_md: A non-composite data type is a type defined **without referencing another data type**.

front_blocks.md: Define **composite data type**.

back_blocks.md: A composite data type is one that **references other data types** in its definition, grouped under a single identifier.

cards.front_md: Define **composite data type**.
cards.back_md: A composite data type is one that **references other data types** in its definition, grouped under a single identifier.

front_blocks.md: What decides whether a type is composite or non-composite?

back_blocks.md: Whether the type **references other data types**, not whether it holds one value or many.

cards.front_md: What decides whether a type is composite or non-composite?
cards.back_md: Whether the type **references other data types**, not whether it holds one value or many.

front_blocks.md: Name the two non-composite user-defined types.

back_blocks.md: **Enumerated** and **pointer**.

cards.front_md: Name the two non-composite user-defined types.
cards.back_md: **Enumerated** and **pointer**.

front_blocks.md: Define **enumerated data type**.

back_blocks.md: An enumerated data type is a non-composite, user-defined type consisting of a list of **all possible values** the variable can take.

cards.front_md: Define **enumerated data type**.
cards.back_md: An enumerated data type is a non-composite, user-defined type consisting of a list of **all possible values** the variable can take.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The values of an enumerated type are unordered.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The values are **ordered**, with an implied sequence based on the order they are declared, so comparisons work.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The values of an enumerated type are unordered.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

The values are **ordered**, with an implied sequence based on the order they are declared, so comparisons work.

front_blocks.md: Why does the order of values matter in an enumerated type?

back_blocks.md: The values are **ordered** by the sequence in which they are declared, so **comparisons work**, for example Monday comes before Tuesday.

cards.front_md: Why does the order of values matter in an enumerated type?
cards.back_md: The values are **ordered** by the sequence in which they are declared, so **comparisons work**, for example Monday comes before Tuesday.

front_blocks.md: What is the pseudocode syntax for an enumerated type?

back_blocks.md: `TYPE <identifier> = (value1, value2, value3, ...)`

cards.front_md: What is the pseudocode syntax for an enumerated type?
cards.back_md: `TYPE <identifier> = (value1, value2, value3, ...)`

front_blocks.md: Define **pointer data type**.

back_blocks.md: A pointer is a non-composite, user-defined type that **stores a memory address only**, rather than the data itself.

cards.front_md: Define **pointer data type**.
cards.back_md: A pointer is a non-composite, user-defined type that **stores a memory address only**, rather than the data itself.

front_blocks.md: What does a pointer definition also indicate?

back_blocks.md: The **type of data stored at that memory location**.

cards.front_md: What does a pointer definition also indicate?
cards.back_md: The **type of data stored at that memory location**.

front_blocks.md: What is the pseudocode syntax for a pointer type?

back_blocks.md: `TYPE <identifier> = ^<data type>`

cards.front_md: What is the pseudocode syntax for a pointer type?
cards.back_md: `TYPE <identifier> = ^<data type>`

front_blocks.md: What are pointers used to build?

back_blocks.md: **Dynamic data structures** such as linked lists.

front_blocks.md: Name the three composite user-defined types.

back_blocks.md: **Record**, **set** and **class**.

cards.front_md: Name the three composite user-defined types.
cards.back_md: **Record**, **set** and **class**.

front_blocks.md: Define **record** as a composite type.

back_blocks.md: A record is a composite type that groups a **fixed number of related items (fields)**, which may be of **different data types**, into a single new type.

cards.front_md: Define **record** as a composite type.
cards.back_md: A record is a composite type that groups a **fixed number of related items (fields)**, which may be of **different data types**, into a single new type.

front_blocks.md: A record groups a <u>**          **</u> number of related fields under one identifier.

back_blocks.md: A record groups a **fixed** number of related fields under one identifier.

cards.front_md: A record groups a <u>**          **</u> number of related fields under one identifier.
cards.back_md: A record groups a **fixed** number of related fields under one identifier.

front_blocks.md: How do you access a field of a record?

back_blocks.md: Using **dot notation**, written as `RecordName.FieldName`.

cards.front_md: How do you access a field of a record?
cards.back_md: Using **dot notation**, written as `RecordName.FieldName`.

front_blocks.md: Define **set**.

back_blocks.md: A set is a composite type holding a list of **unordered elements**, where all elements must be of the **same data type**.

cards.front_md: Define **set**.
cards.back_md: A set is a composite type holding a list of **unordered elements**, where all elements must be of the **same data type**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A set can hold elements of different data types.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
**All elements must be of the same data type**, and the set definition includes the data type it uses.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A set can hold elements of different data types.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

**All elements must be of the same data type**, and the set definition includes the data type it uses.

front_blocks.md: Which operations can be applied to a set?

back_blocks.md: **Set theory operations** such as **union** and **intersection**.

cards.front_md: Which operations can be applied to a set?
cards.back_md: **Set theory operations** such as **union** and **intersection**.

front_blocks.md: What is the pseudocode syntax for declaring a set type?

back_blocks.md: `TYPE <identifier> = SET OF <data type>`

cards.front_md: What is the pseudocode syntax for declaring a set type?
cards.back_md: `TYPE <identifier> = SET OF <data type>`

front_blocks.md: Which keyword tests whether a value is in a set?

back_blocks.md: `ISIN`

cards.front_md: Which keyword tests whether a value is in a set?
cards.back_md: `ISIN`

front_blocks.md: Define **class** as a composite type.

back_blocks.md: A class is a composite type that groups together both **data (attributes)** and the **methods** that operate on that data, under a single identifier.

cards.front_md: Define **class** as a composite type.
cards.back_md: A class is a composite type that groups together both **data (attributes)** and the **methods** that operate on that data, under a single identifier.

front_blocks.md: What is a class used as?

back_blocks.md: A **template to create objects** in object-oriented programming.

cards.front_md: What is a class used as?
cards.back_md: A **template to create objects** in object-oriented programming.

back_blocks.md: An **enumerated type**.

cards.front_md: Which user-defined type suits data that can only be one of a fixed, named list of values?

front_blocks.md: Which user-defined type suits an unordered collection with no duplicates?

back_blocks.md: A **set**.
